claim: Force-induced unfolding and refolding of proteins is speculated to be a key mechanism in the sensing and transduction of mechanical signals in the living cell.
source: The force-induced unfolding and refolding of proteins is speculated to be a key mechanism in the sensing and transduction of mechanical signals in the living cell.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general scientific hypothesis that motivates the study.

claim: Little evidence has been gathered for force-induced unfolding and refolding of proteins in vivo.
source: Yet, little evidence has been gathered for its existence in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Stretch-induced unfolding is postulated to be the activation mechanism of the twitchin/titin family of autoinhibited sarcomeric kinases.
source: Prominently, stretch-induced unfolding is postulated to be the activation mechanism of the twitchin/titin family of autoinhibited sarcomeric kinases linked to the mechanical stress response of muscle.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an existing hypothesis in the field.

claim: Transgenic C. elegans expressing twitchin containing FRET moieties flanking the kinase domain were generated.
source: To test the occurrence of mechanical kinase activation in living working muscle, we generated transgenic Caenorhabditis elegans expressing twitchin containing FRET moieties flanking the kinase domain
evidence: This describes the experimental approach taken in the study.

claim: A quantitative technique for extracting FRET signals in freely moving C. elegans was developed using tracking and simultaneous imaging in three channels.
source: developed a quantitative technique for extracting FRET signals in freely moving C. elegans, using tracking and simultaneous imaging of animals in three channels (donor fluorescence, acceptor fluorescence, and transmitted light).
evidence: This describes the methodological development in the study.

claim: Computer vision algorithms were used to extract fluorescence signals and muscle contraction states in each frame.
source: Computer vision algorithms were used to extract fluorescence signals and muscle contraction states in each frame, in order to obtain fluorescence and body curvature measurements with spatial and temporal precision in vivo.
evidence: This describes the computational methods used in the study.

claim: Statistically significant periodic changes in FRET signals during muscle activity were observed.
source: The data revealed statistically significant periodic changes in FRET signals during muscle activity, consistent with a periodic change in the conformation of twitchin kinase.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: Stretch-unfolding of twitchin kinase occurs in active muscle.
source: We conclude that stretch-unfolding of twitchin kinase occurs in the active muscle, whereby mechanical activity titrates the signaling pathway of this cytoskeletal kinase.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: The methods developed could be applied to obtaining in vivo evidence for force-induced conformational changes of other proteins in C. elegans and other optically transparent animals.
source: We anticipate that the methods we have developed here could be applied to obtaining in vivo evidence for force-induced conformational changes or elastic behavior of other proteins not only in C. elegans but in other animals in which there is optical transparency (e.g., zebrafish).
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about potential applications of the methodology.

claim: Proteins can act as mechanotransductors by undergoing repeated cycles of unfolding and refolding when subjected to directional forces.
source: Accumulating evidence suggests that proteins can act as mechanotransductors by undergoing repeated cycles of unfolding and refolding when subjected to directional forces (Hu et al., 2017; Sharma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: Multi-domain proteins can bear the unfolding of mechanolabile segments while maintaining structural integrity of other functional regions.
source: This mechanism appears to apply in particular to multi-domain proteins that can bear the unfolding of mechanolabile segments of their chains, while maintaining the structural integrity of their other functional regions (Sharma et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: The feasibility of stretch-unfolding in proteins is evidenced by in vitro and computational studies using AFM, optical tweezers, and steered molecular dynamics simulations.
source: The feasibility of such stretch-unfolding in proteins is evidenced by numerous in vitro and computational studies that use atomic force microscopy (AFM), optical tweezers, and steered molecular dynamics simulations (SMDS) (reviewed in Batchelor et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Little evidence of force-induced unfolding in vivo exists to date and its physiological relevance remains strongly debated.
source: However, little evidence of the existence of this mechanism in vivo exists to date and, thus, its physiological relevance remains strongly debated.
evidence: This describes the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: Giant proteins of the twitchin/titin family are key force-sensing molecules in the sarcomere.
source: Mounting evidence indicates that the giant proteins of the twitchin/titin family (0.7–4 MDa) are key force-sensing molecules in the sarcomere (e.g. Butler and Siegman, 2011; Buyandelger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: Twitchin/titin family proteins form elastic intrasarcomeric filaments and contain one or two kinase domains.
source: These proteins form elastic intrasarcomeric filaments and contain one or two kinase domains, which are thought to mediate the response of muscle to mechanical stress (Kontrogianni-Konstantopoulos et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: Nematode twitchin kinase is the closest homolog to human titin kinase.
source: Nematode twitchin kinase (TwcK) is the best studied member of the family and is the closest homolog to human titin kinase (TK).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the relationship between these proteins.

claim: TwcK 3D-structure shows that the kinase domain is enwrapped by N- and C-terminal tail extensions (NL and CRD) that bind against the kinase hinge region and active site, leading to complete inhibition of phosphotransfer activity.
source: TwcK 3D-structure shows that the kinase domain is enwrapped by N- and C-terminal tail extensions (termed NL and CRD) that bind against the kinase hinge region and active site, respectively, leading to a complete inhibition of its phosphotransfer activity (Hu et al., 1994; Lei et al., 1994; von Castelmur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: Truncation of the NL and/or CRD extensions results in active TwcK.
source: The truncation of the NL and/or CRD extensions has been shown to result in active TwcK (von Castelmur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: Human TK shares its 3D-architecture with TwcK.
source: Human TK shares its 3D-architecture with TwcK (Mayans et al., 1998; Bogomolovas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies.

claim: AFM data and SMDS have led to the proposal that the regulatory tails of TwcK and TK are extensible, becoming dynamically and reversibly unfolded by pulling forces during muscle contractile activity.
source: AFM data and SMDS have led to the proposal that the regulatory tails of TwcK and TK are extensible, becoming dynamically and reversibly unfolded by the pulling forces that develop in the sarcomere during muscle contractile activity (von Castelmur et al., 2012; Gräter et al., 2005; Puchner et al., 2008; Puchner and Gaub, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to AFM and computational studies.

claim: Stretch-unfolding of TwcK flanking tails would expose the catalytic center in the kinase and lead to its phosphotransfer activation.
source: The stretch-unfolding of TwcK flanking tails would expose the catalytic center in the kinase and, thereby, lead to its phosphotransfer activation.
evidence: This is a mechanistic hypothesis based on structural and biophysical data.

claim: In Mytilus permeabilized smooth muscles, a 10% stretch resulted in a twofold increase in phosphorylation of a model substrate for molluscan TwcK in vitro.
source: The view that stretch activates TwcK has been supported in Mytilus; using permeabilized smooth muscles, a 10% stretch resulted in a twofold increase in phosphorylation of a model substrate for molluscan TwcK in vitro (Butler and Siegman, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an experimental study.

claim: TwcK phosphotransfer catalysis regulates muscle contraction in C. elegans.
source: For Caenorhabditis elegans, TwcK phosphotransfer catalysis has been revealed to regulate muscle contraction (Matsunaga et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: TwcK is the target of the MAK-1/p38 MAPK pathway linked to cellular stress.
source: TwcK has been shown to be the target of the MAK-1/p38 MAPK pathway that is linked to cellular stress, so that TwcK is hypothesized to be the avenue by which stress factors affect muscle mechanics in C. elegans (Matsunaga et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: Human TK is associated with autophagosomal receptors nbr1 and p62 and E3 ubiquitin ligases MuRF1 and MuRF2.
source: Human TK has been shown to be associated with the autophagosomal receptors nbr1 and p62 and the E3 ubiquitin ligases MuRF1 and MuRF2 and, thereby, it has been linked to turn-over and gene expression patterns in the myofibril in function of mechanical activity (Lange et al., 2005; Bogomolovas et al., 2014; Bogomolovas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: The mechanosensing properties of sarcomeric kinases are speculated to link the proteostatic response of the myofibril to mechanical demand imposed on the sarcomere.
source: Hence, the mechanosensing properties of these sarcomeric kinases are speculated to link the proteostatic response of the myofibril to the mechanical demand imposed on the sarcomere.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the functional role of these kinases.

claim: The kinase region of twitchin from C. elegans is a multi-domain segment with composition Fn-NL-kinase-CRD-Ig.
source: The kinase region of the twitchin protein from C. elegans is a multi-domain segment of composition Fn-NL-kinase-CRD-Ig, where Fn is a fibronectin domain, NL is a 45-residue sequence, CRD is a 60-residue sequence, and Ig is an immunoglobulin domain (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the domain architecture of the protein, with reference to Figure 1A.

claim: NL and CRD sequences bind onto the catalytic kinase domain, inhibiting its catalysis.
source: NL and CRD sequences bind onto the catalytic kinase domain, inhibiting its catalysis (von Castelmur et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a structural study.

claim: A multi-domain kinase chimera carrying fluorescent proteins inserted N- and C-terminally to the NL-Kin-CRD assembly was constructed to act as a FRET stretch sensor in vivo.
source: In order to monitor the unfolding of NL and/or CRD sequences induced by sarcomeric stretch and, thereby, the freeing of twitchin kinase, we constructed a multi-domain kinase chimera carrying fluorescent proteins (FPs) inserted N- and C-terminally to the NL-Kin-CRD assembly, to act as a FRET stretch sensor in vivo.
evidence: This describes the experimental design of the FRET construct.

claim: The resulting chimera had the domain composition Fn-mCitrineFP-NL-TwcK-CRD-mCyanFP-Ig (TwcK-FRET).
source: The resulting chimera had the domain composition Fn-mCitrineFP-NL-TwcK-CRD-mCyanFP-Ig (abbreviated in the following as TwcK-FRET; Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the specific construct design, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: Two loci were selected for FP insertion: a flexible seven-residue segment in the frontal fraction of the NL sequence (6207-DERKRRR-6213) and a two-residue motif (6584-QP-6585) in the linker sequence between CRD and domain Ig26.
source: Specifically, two loci were selected: a flexible seven-residue segment in the frontal fraction of the NL sequence (6207-DERKRRR-6213); and a two-residue motif (6584-QP-6585) in the linker sequence between CRD and domain Ig26.
evidence: This describes the specific sites chosen for FP insertion.

claim: The selected sites for FP insertion were located at a distance of ~5.3 nm, roughly coincident with the 4.8 nm Förster distance of the introduced FP pair.
source: These sites were located at a respective distance of ~5.3 nm (roughly coincident with the 4.8 nm Förster distance of the introduced FP pair Lam et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the distance between FRET moieties and cites a reference for the Förster distance.

claim: mCitrine and mCyan FP are enhanced variants of green FP from Aequorea victoria.
source: Both FPs are enhanced variants of the green FP from Aequorea victoria (Griesbeck et al., 2001; Zacharias et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies describing these fluorescent proteins.

claim: Both mCitrine and mCyan FP variants are monomeric.
source: Important for the present work is that both FP variants are monomeric (Shaner et al., 2005), which minimizes the risk of undesirable mutual interactions within the sarcomeric lattice.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: mCyan FP is a cyan FP that acts as FRET donor and has λEx/λEm maxima at 433/475 nm.
source: mCyan FP (mCFP) is a cyan FP that acts as FRET donor and has λEx/λEm maxima at 433/475 nm.
evidence: This describes the spectral properties of mCFP.

claim: mCitrine FP is an enhanced yellow FP that acts as FRET acceptor, having λEx/λEm maxima at 516/529 nm.
source: The mCitrine FP is an enhanced yellow FP that acts as FRET acceptor, having λEx/λEm maxima at 516/529 nm.
evidence: This describes the spectral properties of mCitrine.

claim: TwcK-mCFP and TwcK-mCitrineFP samples have negligible activity, equivalent to that of wild-type multi-domain TwcK (ca 0.5% of the maximal activity of the free kinase domain).
source: In this study, catalytic assays showed that both TwcK-mCFP and TwcK-mCitrineFP samples have negligible activity, equivalent to that of wild-type multi-domain TwcK (ca 0.5% of the maximal activity of the free kinase domain) (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The insertion of FP proteins flanking TwcK for engineering a FRET sensor did not cause an undesirable perturbation of the native structure of the multidomain kinase.
source: This proved that the insertion of FP proteins flanking TwcK for the purpose of engineering a FRET sensor had not caused an undesirable perturbation of the native structure of the multidomain kinase.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the activity assay data.

claim: Transgenic C. elegans strains were generated expressing multi-domain TwcK-FRET segments.
source: To monitor the FRET signal of the modified TwcK in vivo, C. elegans strains were generated using two different strategies. First, we created transgenic strains expressing multi-domain TwcK-FRET segments similar to those designed and validated biochemically (Figure 1).
evidence: This describes the generation of transgenic strains.

claim: CRISPR/Cas9 was used to edit the twitchin gene to express full-length twitchin containing mCitrineFP and mCFP moieties at normal levels from the endogenous twitchin gene.
source: Once the methodology had been established, and to overcome the potential risk of the overexpressed fragments not mimicking the behavior of the twitchin protein in its native sarcomere context, we used CRISPR/Cas9 to edit the twitchin gene to express full-length twitchin containing mCitrineFP and mCFP moieties positioned as in the tested fragments, and expressed at normal levels from the endogenous twitchin gene.
evidence: This describes the generation of a CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: Endogenous twitchin localizes to sarcomeric A-bands in a characteristic manner with a lack of localization in the middle of A-bands.
source: Endogenous twitchin localizes to sarcomeric A-bands in a characteristic manner in which there is a lack of localization in the middle of A-bands (Moerman et al., 1988).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: A minimal twitchin fragment Ig-Ig-Fn-NL-Kin-CRD-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig displayed normal twitchin A-band localization.
source: Using anti-HA antibodies to visualize the fragments (Figure 2A), we identified a minimal twitchin fragment that displayed normal twitchin A-band localization: Ig-Ig-Fn-NL-Kin-CRD-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The fragment Ig-Ig-Fn-mCitrineFP-NL-Kin-CRD-mCFP-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig localized normally to A-bands when expressed in transgenic worms (strain GB282).
source: The resulting fragment, Ig-Ig-Fn-mCitrineFP-NL-Kin-CRD-mCFP-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig-Ig, also localized normally to A-bands when expressed in transgenic worms (strain GB282) (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A control transgenic animal was created expressing a fragment carrying FRET moieties placed on either side of Ig domain Ig28 (strain GB284).
source: As a 'negative control,' we created a transgenic animal expressing the same minimally localizing fragment but carrying FRET moieties placed on either side of an Ig domain C-terminal to the kinase domain, Ig28 (strain GB284) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This describes the generation of a control strain, with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: AFM measurements have confirmed that Ig28 has a mechanically stable fold and will undergo stretch-induced unfolding only under extreme force.
source: However, AFM measurements have confirmed that Ig28 has a mechanically stable fold and that it will undergo stretch-induced unfolding only under extreme force (Greene et al., 2008), making this a non-extensible construction so that its FRET moieties are not expected to alter significantly their mutual distance at physiological muscle force.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to an AFM study.

claim: The distance between FRET loci in the control Ig28 variant is 4.5–5 nm.
source: Ig28 is a type-I immunoglobulin domain joined serially to its flanking domains by short linker sequences, so that the distance between the FRET loci in this variant is 4.5–5 nm.
evidence: This describes the structural properties of the control construct.

claim: The distances between FRET moieties in the control and test constructs are comparable.
source: Hence, the distances between FRET moieties in the control and test constructs in this study are comparable (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between constructs, with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: The control sample Ig-Ig-Fn-NL-Kin-CRD-Ig-Ig-mCFP-Ig-mCitrineFP-Ig-Ig localized correctly to A-bands when expressed in transgenic worms.
source: The control sample Ig-Ig-Fn-NL-Kin-CRD-Ig-Ig-mCFP-Ig-mCitrineFP-Ig-Ig, when expressed in transgenic worms, also localized correctly to A-bands (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The control strain GB284 expressed twofold higher FP-labeled twitchin segments than the tester strain GB282.
source: To quantitate the expression of test and control twitchin segments in strains GB282 and GB284, respectively, we performed quantitative western blots using total protein extracts and anti-HA antibodies. As shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1, the control strain GB284 expressed twofold higher FP-labeled twitchin segments than the tester strain GB282 (with N=4, mean=2.10).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The divergence in protein expression levels between GB282 and GB284 would not affect the calculated FRET signal directly because the study is based on ratiometric FRET differences.
source: Importantly, as our study is based on ratiometric FRET differences, the divergence in protein expression levels would not affect the calculated signal directly.
evidence: This is a methodological consideration about the ratiometric nature of FRET measurements.

claim: Only the FP labels in the test construct would be expected to alter their FRET signal significantly during muscle function.
source: Only the FP labels in the test construct would be expected to alter their FRET signal significantly during muscle function as the NL and the CRD are the only extensible segments in this twitchin fragment
evidence: This is an expectation based on the design of the constructs.

claim: ΔFRET values would be higher for the test strain than the control strain independently of protein expression levels.
source: and thus, our expectation was that ΔFRET values would be higher for the test than the control strain independently of protein expression levels.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the experimental design.

claim: Local curvature is a good proxy for the mechanical state of the sarcomere in C. elegans.
source: C. elegans move in an undulatory motion most of the time (with a periodicity of ~1 Hz) and its body wall muscle lies directly under the cuticle and is attached to the cuticle via a basement membrane and a thin hypodermal or skin cell layer. Thus, we reasoned that local curvature is a good proxy for the mechanical state of the sarcomere.
evidence: This is a reasoning based on the anatomy and locomotion of C. elegans.

claim: Positive curvature values represent contracted muscles, and negative curvature values represent relaxed and stretched muscles.
source: We defined positive curvature values to represent contracted muscles, and negative curvature values to represent relaxed and stretched muscles.
evidence: This describes the definition used in the analysis.

claim: A tracking platform was integrated with FRET imaging capability to enable single-animal tracking with simultaneous FRET measurement.
source: We integrated a previously developed tracking system (Stirman et al., 2011; Stirman et al., 2012) with a separate newly developed FRET imaging capability (Figure 3, Video 1).
evidence: This describes the technical platform developed for the study, with reference to Figure 3 and Video 1.

claim: The microscope-based platform uses two cameras to enable single-animal tracking in bright-field mode while maintaining the animal in the FOV for FRET measurement.
source: This microscope-based platform uses two cameras to enable single-animal tracking with a large enough field of view in bright-field mode (with enough resolution to measure local curvature), while maintaining the animal in the field of view (FOV) in every frame for FRET measurement (with high enough light collecting power and spatial resolution).
evidence: This describes the technical capabilities of the platform.

claim: The bright-field mode uses a near-infrared (NIR) light source to minimize interference with fluorescence imaging.
source: The bright-field mode uses a near-infrared (NIR) light source to minimize interference with fluorescence imaging (Figure 3A, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes a technical feature of the platform, with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: NIR and FRET images are precision-aligned at the start of the experiments.
source: NIR and FRET images are precision-aligned at the start of the experiments.
evidence: This describes a procedural step in the experiments.

claim: The outline of the worm is calculated frame-by-frame from the bright-field image, and the FRET signal can be mapped to the body and correlated with local curvature.
source: The outline of the worm is exactly calculated frame-by-frame from the bright-field image, and the FRET signal can then be mapped to the body (via pre-experiment alignment) and thus accurately correlated with local curvature (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the analysis approach.

claim: The system uses an LCD-projector as a light source, which allows simultaneous and individual control of excitation bands.
source: The system uses an LCD-projector as a light source, which allows simultaneous and individual control of excitation bands (Stirman et al., 2011; Stirman et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes a technical feature of the platform, with citations to previous work.

claim: A specialized filter set in combination with blue light from the projector was used to excite the donor mCFP, and a beam splitter was used to simultaneously image emissions of both mCFP and mCitrineFP.
source: In order to image the donor and acceptor fluorophores in the transgenic animals, we used a specialized filter set in combination with the blue light source from the projector to excite the donor mCFP, and used a beam splitter to simultaneously image the emissions of both the donor mCFP and the acceptor mCitrineFP (see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the optical setup for FRET imaging.

claim: Fluorescence imaging was performed with an EMCCD camera at a frame rate of 20 fps.
source: Fluorescence imaging was then performed with an EMCCD camera, with a frame rate of 20 fps.
evidence: This describes a technical parameter of the imaging system.

claim: By using a 5× objective, the spatial resolution of measurements is limited by the camera, resulting in 3.125 μm/px.
source: By using a 5× objective to give a large FOV to capture the entire worm body, the spatial resolution of measurements is thus limited by the camera, which results in 3.125 μm/px.
evidence: This describes the spatial resolution of the imaging system.

claim: The system has low photobleaching due to illumination at low magnification, allowing imaging for longer periods of time.
source: A key benefit of this system is the low amount of photobleaching due to the illumination at low magnification, allowing for imaging for longer periods of time.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the imaging approach.

claim: Animals expressed a bright GFP marker in the pharynx (using the myo-2 promoter), which allowed maintaining the animal in the center of the FOV.
source: Additionally, in our experiments animals expressed a bright GFP marker in the pharynx (using the myo-2 promoter), which allowed us to maintain the animal in the center of the FOV.
evidence: This describes a technical feature used for tracking.

claim: Tracking and stage updates were at 10 Hz, which is fast enough to maintain the animal in the FOV at all times.
source: Tracking and stage updates were at 10 Hz, which is fast enough to maintain the animal in the FOV at all times, even during fast forward locomotion.
evidence: This describes the tracking performance of the system.

claim: Point set registration was used to align each fluorescence frame to a bright-field frame, allowing accurate comparisons of fluorescence signals and body postures.
source: By using point set registration, we aligned each fluorescence frame to a bright-field frame, allowing for accurate comparisons of fluorescence signals and body postures (Figure 3B).
evidence: This describes the image alignment method, with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The platform is capable of automatic tracking of worms with simultaneous two-color fluorescence imaging, with a spatial resolution of ~3 μm and temporal resolution of 50 ms.
source: This platform is therefore capable of automatic tracking of worms with simultaneous two-color fluorescence imaging, with a spatial resolution of ~3 μm and temporal resolution of 50 ms.
evidence: This summarizes the capabilities of the platform.

claim: The platform enables imaging of freely moving animals expressing FRET moieties over a prolonged period of time (>90 s) to allow for correlational analyses.
source: Thereby, this platform enables imaging of freely moving animals expressing FRET moieties and does so over a prolonged period of time (>90 s) to allow for correlational analyses.
evidence: This describes the duration of imaging possible with the platform.

claim: An automated analysis pipeline was developed to extract FRET signals and muscle contraction states from each frame with spatial specificity along the length of the animal.
source: We next developed an automated analysis pipeline to extract FRET signals and muscle contraction states from each frame of the recorded videos, with spatial specificity along the length of the animal accurately and without bias (Figure 3C).
evidence: This describes the analysis pipeline, with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: The bright-field NIR channel image has high contrast between background and foreground, allowing for robust and smooth segmentation of the body outline.
source: For each set of frames, we used the bright-field NIR channel image, which has a high contrast between background and foreground, allowing for robust and smooth segmentation of the body outline (Figure 3D).
evidence: This describes a feature of the image analysis, with reference to Figure 3D.

claim: The binary image of the body outline was used to create an ordered set of points along the midline of the worm, from head to tail.
source: The binary image of the body outline was used to create an ordered set of points along the midline of the worm, from head to tail.
evidence: This describes a step in the image analysis pipeline.

claim: The midline spline and body outline were used to create individual binary mask images of the dorsal and ventral sides of the animal.
source: The midline spline and the body outline were subsequently used to create individual binary mask images of the dorsal and ventral sides of the animal.
evidence: This describes a step in the image analysis pipeline.

claim: Ventral and dorsal sides of the worm body were tracked and treated separately and assigned opposite curvature values.
source: Ventral and dorsal sides of the worm body were tracked and treated separately and assigned opposite curvature values (Figure 3Ei).
evidence: This describes the analysis approach, with reference to Figure 3Ei.

claim: Muscle contraction states were characterized by normalized curvature measurements.
source: Muscle contraction states were then characterized by normalized curvature measurements
evidence: This describes how muscle contraction was quantified.

claim: FRET signals were computed from extracted mCFP and mCitrineFP emission intensities from the corresponding fluorescence recordings.
source: while FRET signals were computed from extracted mCFP and mCitrineFP emission intensities from the corresponding fluorescence recordings (Figure 3Eii, iii, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes how FRET was quantified, with reference to Figure 3Eii and iii.

claim: Angles between the center of mass of each segmented side and the midline of the animal were computed to robustly track the two sides throughout recordings.
source: To robustly track the two sides throughout recordings, we computed the angles between the center of mass of each segmented side and the midline of the animal (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, and see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the method for tracking dorsal and ventral sides, with reference to Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: This process allowed robust assignment of consistent labels to the two sides of the animal continuously throughout recordings with an accuracy of >90%.
source: This process allowed us to robustly assign consistent labels to the two sides of the animal continuously throughout recordings with an accuracy of >90%, with the majority of incorrectly assigned labels occurring in frames during stage movements.
evidence: This describes the performance of the side-tracking algorithm.

claim: Most of the time the animals moved forward with a traveling wave propagating backward, and curvature values showed clear and smooth diagonal patterns.
source: As expected, most of the time the animals moved forward with a traveling wave propagating backward, and curvature values showing clear and smooth diagonal patterns (Figure 4A), similar to recorded kymographs in other studies (Wen et al., 2012; Fouad et al., 2018; Gao et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes observations from the data, with reference to Figure 4A and citations to other studies.

claim: mCFP and mCitrineFP emission measurements extracted as a function of both time and distance along the worm body showed wave-like patterns.
source: Similarly, mCFP and mCitrineFP emission measurements extracted as a function of both time and distance along the worm body also showed wave-like patterns (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This describes observations from the data, with reference to Figures 4B and C.

claim: Fluorescence measurements were more variable between animals and along the anterior-posterior axis of the animal, and had a lower signal-to-noise ratio compared to curvature measurements.
source: In comparison to curvature measurements, fluorescence measurements were more variable between animals and along the anterior-posterior axis of the animal, and had a lower signal-to-noise ratio.
evidence: This describes a characteristic of the fluorescence data.

claim: The variability in fluorescence measurements is due to uneven expression level of the transgene in different regions, varying body diameter introducing optical artifacts, and autofluorescence.
source: This is due to the uneven expression level of the transgene in different regions, the diameter of the body varying (and thus introducing optical artifacts differentially along the body), and autofluorescence.
evidence: This provides an explanation for the observed variability in fluorescence.

claim: Fluorescence measurements seemed to reflect the patterns of muscle contractions, suggesting that FRET and curvature of the muscle are related.
source: Nonetheless, fluorescence measurements seemed to reflect the patterns of muscle contractions. This suggests that FRET and curvature of the muscle are related.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed patterns in the data.

claim: When examining curvature and fluorescence signals for each individual segment, oscillatory patterns with similar frequencies were observed for all signals.
source: Significantly, when examining the curvature and fluorescence signals for each individual segment, we observed oscillatory patterns with similar frequencies for all signals (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: This describes observations from the data, with reference to Figures 4D and E.

claim: The consistency between fluorescence signals and curvature dynamics of freely moving animals suggests that the relationship between these variables is causal.
source: Taken together, the consistency between the fluorescence signals and curvature dynamics of freely moving animals suggests that the relationship between these variables is causal.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the consistency of the observations.

claim: The twitchin constructions were designed to yield maximal FRET signal in the absence of stretch as the protein segments will be compacted, while the FRET signal will be reduced upon stretch if parts of the twitchin segment undergo force-induced unfolding.
source: The twitchin constructions in this work have been designed to yield maximal FRET signal in the absence of stretch as the protein segments will then be compacted, while the FRET signal will be reduced upon stretch if parts of the twitchin segment undergo force-induced unfolding.
evidence: This describes the design principle of the FRET constructs.

claim: The inextensible control (GB284) was designed to report on inherent locomotion artifacts, noise, and effects derived from internal sarcomere rearrangements during motion.
source: The inextensible control (GB284) was designed to report on inherent locomotion artifacts, noise, and effects derived from internal sarcomere rearrangements during motion; this ensures that the differences in the measurements between strains can be attributed to conformational changes in twitchin kinase.
evidence: This describes the purpose of the control construct.

claim: Changes in signal were obtained by averaging thousands of measurements, which would remove non-systematic variability in the observations.
source: In addition, changes in signal were obtained in this study by averaging thousands of measurements (see Materials and methods), which would remove non-systematic variability in the observations, such as FRET differences resulting from dynamic orientations of fluorophores.
evidence: This describes the statistical approach used to reduce noise.

claim: An increase in both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities during muscle contractions was observed in the control strain GB284.
source: Although the expectation was that the FRET signal from the control GB284 would remain relatively constant, we observed FRET variations, including an increase in both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities during muscle contractions (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: This describes observations from the control strain, with reference to Figures 5A-D.

claim: The variation in FRET signal in GB284 was interpreted to result from optical nonlinearities, instrument artifacts, and/or possible inter-molecular interactions between FRET moieties in adjacent molecules in the sarcomeric lattice.
source: We interpreted the variation to result from optical nonlinearities in the recorded emission intensities, instrument artifacts due to hardware motoring during worm tracking and/or possible inter-molecular interactions between FRET moieties in adjacent molecules in the sarcomeric lattice.
evidence: This provides an interpretation of the observed variation in the control.

claim: A likely explanation for the observed increase in both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities during muscle contractions is that fluorophores become more densely packed in space during contractions.
source: Indeed, a likely explanation for the observed increase in both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities during muscle contractions is that fluorophores become more densely packed in space during contractions, leading to increased quantifications of fluorescence emissions as a result of locomotion.
evidence: This provides a mechanistic explanation for the observed intensity changes.

claim: The control strain GB284 reported on all changes in the FRET signal that were due to causes other than the stretch-induced unfolding of the twitchin chain.
source: In brief, the control strain reported on all changes in the FRET signal that were due to causes other than the stretch-induced unfolding of the twitchin chain.
evidence: This summarizes the purpose of the control strain.

claim: Increases in both mCFP and mCitrine intensities during muscle contractions were also observed in the test strain GB282.
source: Next, we examined the test strain GB282. As in GB284, we also observed increases in both mCFP and mCitrine intensities during muscle contractions (Figure 5E–G)
evidence: This describes observations from the test strain, with reference to Figures 5E-G.

claim: GB282 showed statistically significant larger changes in the overall normalized FRET signal compared to GB284.
source: Compared to GB284, GB282 showed statistically significant larger changes in the overall normalized FRET signal (compare Figure 5D and H).
evidence: This is a key finding comparing test and control strains, with reference to Figures 5D and H.

claim: The larger change in the normalized FRET signal for GB282 with respect to the inextensible control GB284 suggests that FRET fluorophores flanking the kinase domain undergo a change in their mutual distancing during muscle function.
source: Since the relative distances between fluorophores introduced in test and control twitchin segments were similar and the sarcomere context of both constructs was also comparable (Figure 2), the larger change in the normalized FRET signal for GB282 with respect to the inextensible control GB284 suggests that FRET fluorophores flanking the kinase domain undergo a change in their mutual distancing during muscle function that is detectable over other sources of signal variation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of test and control strains.

claim: The result agrees with expectations and points to a stretch-induced conformational change near the kinase domain of twitchin during muscle activity.
source: This result agrees with expectations and points to a stretch-induced conformational change near the kinase domain of twitchin during muscle activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the results in the context of the hypothesis.

claim: The lower range in FRET signal (ΔFRET) in the control GB284 confirmed that the higher level of expression of the fusion protein in GB284 versus GB282 did not affect the result.
source: Moreover, the lower range in FRET signal (ΔFRET) in the control GB284 was as expected and confirmed that the higher level of expression of the fusion protein in GB284 versus the tester strain GB282 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1) did not affect the result.
evidence: This addresses a potential confound related to expression levels, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: For both strains GB282 and GB284, the majority of samples have a maximum correlation at a delay of t=0 between FRET signals and curvature.
source: For both strains, the majority of samples have a maximum correlation at a delay of t=0, suggesting that there is no observable delay between FRET signals and curvature as measured in our imaging platform.
evidence: This describes the cross-correlation analysis results.

claim: The observation that there is no delay between FRET signals and curvature indicates that the response time of the instrumentation is appropriate and did not introduce experimental artifacts.
source: This observation indicates that the response time of our instrumentation is appropriate and that it did not introduce experimental artifacts.
evidence: This is an inference about the instrumentation based on the correlation analysis.

claim: The periodic patterns observed in the cross-correlation plots suggest that the observed positive correlation is due to locomotion, and not arbitrary artifacts.
source: Moreover, the periodic patterns observed in the cross-correlation plots suggest that the observed positive correlation is indeed due to locomotion, and not arbitrary artifacts.
evidence: This is an inference about the source of the correlation based on the pattern.

claim: Positive correlation coefficients for both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities, as well as FRET, were observed in both strains GB282 and GB284.
source: As expected, we observed positive correlation coefficients for both mCFP and mCitrineFP intensities, as well as FRET, in both strains (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C).
evidence: This describes the correlation analysis results, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: The correlation coefficients for mCFP are comparable in GB282 and GB284.
source: Importantly, the correlation coefficients for mCFP are comparable in GB282 and GB284 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C, left)
evidence: This describes a comparison of correlation coefficients, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Correlation coefficients for mCitrineFP and computed FRET are significantly higher for GB282 as compared to GB284.
source: whereas correlation coefficients for mCitrineFP and computed FRET are significantly higher for GB282 as compared to GB284 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2C, middle and right).
evidence: This describes a key difference between test and control strains, with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 2C.

claim: Putative intermolecular sarcomeric effects or other unaccounted sources could only partially explain the variations in FRET in GB282 during muscle function.
source: This suggests that putative intermolecular sarcomeric effects or other unaccounted sources could only partially explain the variations in FRET in GB282 during muscle function
evidence: This is an inference about the sources of FRET variation.

claim: A significant portion of the change in FRET signal in GB282 must arise from conformational changes around the kinase domain.
source: and that a significant portion of the change in FRET signal in GB282 must arise from conformational changes around the kinase domain.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the comparison of test and control strains.

claim: Computed curvature values between GB282 and GB284 do not appear significantly different, indicating that the genetically modified sarcomeres in both strains function similarly.
source: Using this automated analysis, computed curvature values between GB282 and GB284 do not appear significantly different, indicating that the genetically modified sarcomeres in both strains function similarly (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes a comparison of muscle function between strains, with reference to Figure 6A.

claim: Both strains GB282 and GB284 exhibit increases in FRET during muscle contractions and decreases during muscle relaxations, so that the changes in signal are motion dependent in both cases.
source: Both strains exhibit increases in FRET during muscle contractions and decreases during muscle relaxations, so that the changes in signal are motion dependent in both cases.
evidence: This describes a common pattern observed in both strains.

claim: The magnitude of the changes in FRET is significantly higher for GB282 compared to GB284.
source: However, the magnitude of the changes is significantly higher for GB282 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a key finding comparing test and control strains, with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: For each part of the muscle contraction cycle, the magnitudes of the changes in computed FRET were significantly higher for GB282 compared to those for GB284.
source: For each part of the muscle contraction cycle, the magnitudes of the changes in computed FRET were significantly higher for GB282 compared to those for GB284 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This describes a detailed comparison across the contraction cycle, with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Changes in FRET and curvature were positively correlated for all parts of the muscle contraction cycle, with significantly higher correlation coefficients for GB282 compared to GB284.
source: Additionally, changes in FRET and curvature were positively correlated for all parts of the muscle contraction cycle, with significantly higher correlation coefficients for GB282 compared to GB284 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes correlation analysis across the contraction cycle, with reference to Figure 6D.

claim: The FRET signal decreases as the muscle relaxes (from 90° to 270°), and this decrease is much stronger for GB282 than for the control GB284.
source: Most importantly, as is seen in Figure 6B, the FRET signal decreases as the muscle relaxes (from 90° to 270°), and this decrease is much stronger for GB282 than for the control GB284.
evidence: This is a key observation about FRET changes during muscle relaxation, with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: A large portion of the change in the FRET signal from GB282 must arise from the increased extension of the FRET moieties during muscle relaxation, and not simply from sarcomere lattice effects or experimental artifacts.
source: Given this difference in magnitude in the FRET decline between test (GB282) and control (GB284), and that both the test and control constructs had the same backbone and chemical composition and a similar sarcomeric localization, we concluded that a large portion of the change in the FRET signal from GB282 must arise from the increased extension of the FRET moieties, and again not simply from sarcomere lattice effects or experimental artifacts, and this occurs during muscle relaxation.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the comparison of test and control during muscle relaxation.

claim: C. elegans strain GB287 was created using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to insert coding sequences for FRET moieties into the endogenous unc-22 (twitchin) gene.
source: In order to ensure that the changes in FRET in this study report on the physiological response of twitckin kinase in its native sarcomeric context, we created C. elegans strain GB287. This strain was developed using CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to insert coding sequences for the FRET moieties into the endogenous unc-22 (twitchin) gene, in the same positions as in the transgenic line GB282.
evidence: This describes the generation of a CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: The GB287 strain expressed full-length ~750 kDa twitchin with FP proteins flanking the kinase domain.
source: The GB287 strain expressed full-length ~750 kDa twitchin with FP proteins flanking the kinase domain and thus, their sarcomeres carried embedded a FRET reporter system.
evidence: This describes the protein expressed in the CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: Twitchin expression in GB287 is at endogenous levels as the native unc-22 (twitchin) promoter was utilized.
source: Twitchin expression in this strain is at endogenous levels as the native unc-22 (twitchin) promoter was utilized.
evidence: This describes the expression level in the CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: GB287 worms expressed the tagged twitchin in the appropriate cells (body wall and pharyngeal muscle).
source: The GB287 worms expressed the tagged twitchin in the appropriate cells (body wall and pharyngeal muscle) (Figure 7A)
evidence: This describes the expression pattern in GB287, with reference to Figure 7A.

claim: The tagged twitchin in GB287 localized properly to sarcomeric A-bands.
source: and this tagged twitchin localized properly to sarcomeric A-bands (Figure 7B).
evidence: This describes the localization of the tagged protein, with reference to Figure 7B.

claim: GB287 animals displayed normal locomotion.
source: In addition, GB287 animals displayed normal locomotion.
evidence: This describes the phenotype of the CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: Because the FRET moieties in GB287 are expressed from the single copy native unc-22 (twitchin) gene, the fluorescence emissions were much dimmer than those from the transgenic lines, leading to increased noise in quantified FRET signals.
source: Because the FRET moieties are expressed from the single copy native unc-22 (twitchin) gene, the fluorescence emissions were much dimmer than those from the transgenic lines, leading to increased noise in quantified FRET signals.
evidence: This describes a technical challenge with the CRISPR-edited strain.

claim: When computing cross-correlations between curvature and quantified FRET signals in GB287, clear positive correlations with near zero delay were observed.
source: Nevertheless, when computing cross-correlations between curvature and quantified FRET signals in GB287, we observed clear positive correlations with near zero delay (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the correlation analysis for GB287, with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: When comparing FRET changes during muscle contraction cycles in GB287, a similar trend to GB282 was observed, showing positive correlations between FRET changes and curvature for all phases of the cycle.
source: Additionally, when comparing FRET changes during muscle contraction cycles, we observed a similar trend to GB282, showing positive correlations between FRET changes and curvature for all phases of the cycle (Figure 7D–F).
evidence: This describes the FRET changes in GB287 during the contraction cycle, with reference to Figures 7D-F.

claim: The largest and most continuous decrease in FRET in GB287 occurs during muscle relaxation, from ~140° to 225°.
source: Importantly, the largest and most continuous decrease in FRET occurs during muscle relaxation, in this case from ~140° to 225° (Figure 7D)
evidence: This describes a key observation in GB287, with reference to Figure 7D.

claim: The magnitude of the change in the normalized signal in GB287 is higher than in GB282.
source: Notably, the magnitude of the change in the normalized signal (Figure 7D) is higher in GB287 than GB282.
evidence: This compares the magnitude of FRET changes between GB287 and GB282, with reference to Figure 7D.

claim: In GB282, twitchin fragments are overexpressed and incorporated in the sarcomere at over-endogenous levels, so that speculatively intermolecular FRET could occur among neighboring molecules, potentially masking the true intramolecular FRET changes.
source: This is consistent with the notion that in GB282 twitchin fragments are overexpressed and incorporated in the sarcomere at over-endogenous levels, so that speculatively intermolecular FRET could occur among neighboring molecules, potentially masking the true intramolecular FRET changes.
evidence: This provides a speculative explanation for the difference in FRET magnitude between GB282 and GB287.

claim: In GB287, where twitchin filaments are at endogenous levels, intermolecular effects might be decreased, so that the signal variation reports more directly on intramolecular conformational changes.
source: In GB287, where twitchin filaments are at endogenous levels, such intermolecular effects might be decreased, so that the signal variation reports here more directly on intramolecular conformational changes.
evidence: This provides a speculative explanation for why GB287 shows larger FRET changes.

claim: The observed changes in FRET signal in GB287 reproduce the results obtained for GB282.
source: Altogether, the observed changes in FRET signal in GB287 reproduce the results obtained for GB282.
evidence: This summarizes the consistency between GB287 and GB282 results.

claim: The changes in FRET must arise from changes in the intramolecular distance in FRET moieties around the kinase domain.
source: We concluded that the changes must arise from changes in the intramolecular distance in FRET moieties around the kinase domain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the GB287 results.

claim: The FRET signals can be attributed to conformational changes local to the kinase domain of twitchin and enabled by the mechanical liability of the NL and/or CRD tails.
source: Thereby, the signals can be attributed to conformational changes local to the kinase domain of twitchin and enabled by the mechanical liability of the NL and/or CRD tails.
evidence: This is a key conclusion about the mechanism underlying the FRET changes.

claim: Movement effects influenced fluorescence measurements in freely moving animals.
source: In our methodology, movement effects influenced fluorescence measurements in freely moving animals.
evidence: This acknowledges a technical challenge in the measurements.

claim: A measured rise in fluorescence during muscle contraction relative to the slack muscle state appeared to indicate an increased packing density of fluorophores in the contracted sarcomere.
source: First, a measured rise in fluorescence during muscle contraction relative to the slack muscle state appeared to indicate an increased packing density of fluorophores in the contracted sarcomere.
evidence: This provides an interpretation of observed fluorescence changes.

claim: Optical aberrations due to the nearby cuticle or agar likely contributed significantly to the measurements.
source: Additionally, optical aberrations due to the nearby cuticle or agar likely contributed significantly to our measurements.
evidence: This identifies a potential source of artifacts in the measurements.

claim: By using FRET, ratiometric values normalized to the sum of the two fluorophores were computed, which was effective in removing a large portion of movement effects.
source: First, by using FRET, we computed ratiometric values that were normalized to the sum of the two fluorophores. Although this was effective in removing a large portion of such movement products, it only removed linear effects.
evidence: This describes a strategy used to mitigate movement artifacts.

claim: Test and control strains expressing the same twitchin fragment but containing FRET moieties at different locations were compared.
source: Second, we compared test and control strains expressing the same twitchin fragment but containing FRET moieties at different locations.
evidence: This describes the experimental design for controlling artifacts.

claim: Both test and control fragments incorporated equally in the sarcomere, so context-dependent effects can be expected to be similar in both strains.
source: We showed that both fragments incorporated equally in the sarcomere, and thus context-dependent effects—for example, potential FRET arising from intermolecular lattice packing effects in the sarcomere—can be expected to be similar in both strains.
evidence: This is a reasoning about why the control is appropriate.

claim: The increased FRET change in the test strain reflects a change in the position of the FP labels indicative of a conformational extension of the sequences flanking the kinase domain, which exceeds any other movement effects.
source: As the change in FRET signal is substantially larger in the test strain than in the inextensible control, we reasoned that the increased FRET change in the test strain reflects a change in the position of the FP labels indicative of a conformational extension of the sequences flanking the kinase domain, which exceeds any other movement effects.
evidence: This is a key conclusion drawn from the comparison of test and control strains.

claim: By using ratiometric FRET and comparing test and control strains, it was confirmed with statistical significance that conformational extensibility at the TwcK locus takes place at physiological forces in vivo during muscle activity.
source: Thus, by using these two strategies, we were able to confirm with statistical significance that conformational extensibility at the TwcK locus takes place at physiological forces in vivo during muscle activity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study.

claim: Since the FRET method yields an average signal to which a large number of individual molecules contribute, the signal does not inform on individual changes in individual molecules.
source: It must be noted, however, that since the FRET method applied in this study yields an average signal, to which a large number of individual molecules contribute, the signal does not inform on individual changes in individual molecules.
evidence: This is a limitation of the FRET method used.

claim: No information can be inferred on whether unfolding might occur synchronously or asynchronously in the sarcomere.
source: Therefore, no information can be inferred on whether unfolding might occur synchronously or asynchronously in the sarcomere.
evidence: This is a limitation of what can be concluded from the data.

claim: The methodology developed could be applied to obtain in vivo evidence for the presumed elasticity of other muscle proteins, especially giant proteins of the twitchin/titin family.
source: The methodology that we have developed here could be applied to obtain in vivo evidence for the presumed elasticity of other muscle proteins, especially giant proteins of the twitchin/titin family.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about potential applications.

claim: The giant protein UNC-89, homologous to both obscurin and SPEG, has a 647-residue region lying between two protein kinase domains that is likely to be a random coil and acts as a highly elastic spring in AFM pulling experiments in vitro.
source: For example, the giant protein, UNC-89, homologous to both obscurin and SPEG, has a 647-residue region lying between two protein kinase domains. This region is likely to be a random coil and acts as a highly elastic spring in AFM pulling experiments in vitro (Qadota et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to another study.

claim: In-frame deletion of the 647-residue region in UNC-89 results in sarcomeric disorganization.
source: Although in-frame deletion of this region results in sarcomeric disorganization, whether this region behaves elastically in vivo is not known.
evidence: This describes a known phenotype but identifies a gap in knowledge.

claim: The placement of FRET pairs by CRISPR in or around the 647-residue region of UNC-89 could be used to study its behavior with respect to the contraction-relaxation cycle.
source: Thus, the placement of FRET pairs by CRISPR in or around this region could be used to study its behavior with respect to the contraction-relaxation cycle.
evidence: This is a proposed future application of the methodology.

claim: The FRET strategy could be used to study the 2.2 MDa nematode protein TTN-1, which contains multiple segments speculated to be highly elastic.
source: Such a strategy could also be used to study the 2.2 MDa nematode protein TTN-1, which contains multiple segments which are speculated to be highly elastic (Flaherty et al., 2002; Forbes et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a proposed future application, with citations to studies on TTN-1.

claim: The data bring support to the view that sarcomere activity elicits the stretch-induced activation of TwcK.
source: As removal of the NL and/or CRD sequences releases the inhibition of TwcK phosphor-transferase activity (von Castelmur et al., 2012), our data bring support to the view that sarcomere activity elicits the stretch-induced activation of TwcK.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data in the context of prior knowledge.

claim: The data indicate that the kinase activity diminishes during muscle relaxation, suggesting that TwcK might remain in its inhibited state in inactive muscle.
source: As our data indicate that the kinase activity diminishes during muscle relaxation, it might be deduced that TwcK remains in its inhibited state in inactive muscle.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed FRET changes.

claim: A CRISPR-generated twitchin mutant in which TwcK was rendered catalytically inactive resulted in animals that moved faster and their sarcomeres contracted more than those of wild type nematodes.
source: We have reported that a CRISPR-generated twitchin mutant in which TwcK was rendered catalytically inactive resulted in animals that moved faster and, by use of an optogenetic method, their sarcomeres contracted more than those of wild type nematodes (Matsunaga et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a previous study by the authors.

claim: The phosphotransfer activity of TwcK inhibits muscle activity, most likely phosphorylating a substrate that reduces the strength or duration of muscle contraction.
source: This implied that the phosphotransfer activity of TwcK inhibits muscle activity, most likely phosphorylating a substrate that reduces the strength or duration of muscle contraction.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the phenotype of the catalytically inactive mutant.

claim: Muscle activity causes the activation of a TwcK signaling pathway.
source: The results reported here lead us to speculate that muscle activity causes the activation of a TwcK signaling pathway.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the results.

claim: Once the TwcK substrate has become phosphorylated, this phosphorylated substrate might stay and accumulate in the myofibril until the signal is abolished by other means.
source: Potentially, once the TwcK substrate has become phosphorylated (i.e., the signal has been launched in the cell), this phosphorylated substrate might stay and accumulate in the myofibril until the signal is abolished by other means (e.g., action of phosphatases, substrate degradation, or recompartmentalization).
evidence: This is a speculative mechanistic model.

claim: A phosphatase might be part of the sarcomere, perhaps even physically interacting with TwcK.
source: Such a phosphatase might be part of the sarcomere, perhaps even physically interacting with TwcK.
evidence: This is a speculative statement.

claim: UNC-89 (obscurin) has two protein kinase domains, and this region of the molecule interacts with two classes of protein phosphatases, PP2A and SCPL-1 (CTD-type phosphatase).
source: For example, UNC-89 (obscurin) has two protein kinase domains, and this region of the molecule interacts with two classes of protein phosphatases, PP2A (Qadota et al., 2018), and SCPL-1 (CTD-type phosphatase) (Qadota et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: The TwcK signaling cascade might be active in working muscle, with sarcomere activity potentially having a titrating effect on the pathway by modulating the cellular levels of phosphorylated substrate.
source: Thus, speculatively the TwcK signaling cascade might be active in working muscle. Sarcomere activity (i.e., rate of contraction cycles) might potentially have a titrating effect on the pathway by modulating the cellular levels of phosphorylated substrate.
evidence: This is a speculative model of TwcK signaling.

claim: In an inactive muscle, TwcK might remain autoinhibited and its signaling pathway shut down.
source: In an inactive muscle, TwcK might remain autoinhibited and, thereby, its signaling pathway shut down.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about TwcK in inactive muscle.

claim: Human TK is thought to be a largely inactive pseudokinase that serves as scaffold in the recruitment of turn-over protein factors to the sarcomere.
source: Interestingly, human TK, which shares its multi-domain 3D-architecture with TwcK (Bogomolovas et al., 2021), is thought to be a largely inactive pseudokinase (Bogomolovas et al., 2014) that serves as scaffold in the recruitment of turn-over protein factors—MuRF E3 ubiquitin ligases and Nbr1/p62 autophagosomal receptors—to the sarcomere (Lange et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: A stretch-unfolding of TK's NL segment has been proposed to regulate MuRF1-mediated ubiquitination of TK that appears to modulate the targetability of this sarcomeric locus by Nbr1/p62 in response to mechanical stress.
source: Most recently, a similar stretch-unfolding of TK's NL segment has been proposed to regulate MuRF1-mediated ubiquitination of TK that, in turn, appears to modulate the targetability of this sarcomeric locus by Nbr1/p62 in response to mechanical stress (Bogomolovas et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a recent study.

claim: It is tantalizing to envision that TK's scaffolding properties and the targeting of its sarcomeric locus by turn-over factors could be coupled to muscle inactivity via the elastic properties of TK as part of the onset of the atrophic process.
source: Thereby, it is tantalizing to envision that TK's scaffolding properties and, thus, the targeting of its sarcomeric locus by turn-over factors, could be coupled to muscle inactivity via the elastic properties of TK as part of the onset of the atrophic process.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the role of TK in muscle atrophy.

claim: The findings bring support to the view that protein stretch-unfolding of cytoskeletal components is a viable force-sensing mechanism in vivo.
source: In conclusion, our findings bring support to the view that protein stretch-unfolding of cytoskeletal components is a viable force-sensing mechanism in vivo.
evidence: This is the overarching conclusion of the study.

claim: This is the first demonstration of spatiotemporal quantification of FRET within the whole body of freely moving C. elegans.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of spatiotemporal quantification of FRET within the whole body of freely moving C. elegans.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the methodology.

claim: There is a detectable and statistically significant change in FRET signal that correlates with the contraction-relaxation mechanical cycle of muscle as the worm moves.
source: We demonstrate that as the worm moves, there is a detectable and statistically significant change in FRET signal that correlates with the contraction-relaxation mechanical cycle of muscle.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study.

claim: The FRET signal is maximal during muscle contraction and minimal during muscle stretch.
source: The FRET signal is maximal during muscle contraction and minimal during muscle stretch.
evidence: This describes the pattern of FRET changes during the muscle cycle.

claim: Physiological forces acting on twitchin kinase in its native in vivo context are capable of inducing stretch-unfolding events.
source: This suggests that physiological forces acting on twitchin kinase in its native in vivo context are capable of inducing stretch-unfolding events and, thus, that this is a physiologically relevant mechanism in live muscle.
evidence: This is a key conclusion of the study.
